title: Example 113: a nested Billing record on PlaceOrder carries constraints no @Valid leads into, caught by the validation checks of the boundary contract (B12)
description: The first example of the validation checks on a boundary contract: jvmcontract reads the Bean Validation constraints on each wire type of the Box Office ticketing service, inside the types too (from the class file's type annotations), and writes a ! line under a property whose type carries constraints that no @Valid on the property or inside its type leads into, as Hibernate Validator does not cascade without one. The patch adds a nested Billing record with @NotBlank and @Email fields to PlaceOrder as a @NotNull component; the handler's @Valid validates PlaceOrder's own properties only, so a blank name or a bad email is accepted, and every test posts valid ones. The change is intended, so the runner regenerates the contract and reports as the violation the new ! line: constraints on Billing are not checked: no @Valid on billing. The runner compiles the module with Gradle, reads the runtime class path through the build's printRuntimeClasspath task, and runs jvmcontract update then verify with --resources and --classpath; the module's Spring Boot tests need Docker and are recorded as the tests' result.
expected: build.py 113 exits 0: verdict violation, 1 new problem, matches expected
